t.E128.agn: In 2007 the European Commission suspended the use of this colour in food as an emergency measure (Regulation 884/2007). For this reason it is not found in foods produced in the EU. In 2007 EFSA withdrew the acceptable daily intake (ADI) and regarded Red 2G as a safety concern, noting that it is extensively converted to aniline in the body and that aniline has shown genotoxic and carcinogenic effects in rodents.
t.E128.body: In rats and rabbits, orally ingested Red 2G is not found unchanged in urine; the dye is split at the azo bond and excreted in urine mainly as p-aminophenol (mostly conjugated with glucuronic acid), and in smaller amounts as o-aminophenol and aniline.
t.E128.eff.0.t: In 2007 the EU suspended its use in food as an emergency measure; it is not found in foods produced in the EU
t.E128.eval: Its authorisation as a food colour in the EU was withdrawn in 2007.
t.E128.found.0: Not used in food in the EU since 2007
t.E128.prod: An azo dye produced by chemical synthesis.
t.E128.summary: A synthetic, red azo dye. It was formerly used in sausages and burgers.
t.E128.what: Used to give food a red colour.
t.agency.EU_withdrawn_2007: Its use in the EU was suspended.
